title: How long can real polynomial roots avoid a collision?
audience: A self-contained mathematical explanation and practical guide for researchers, programmers and students
meaning: A proved finite-polynomial guarantee and reproducible implementation. Novelty is unestablished; no Riemann Hypothesis or new prime-algorithm result is claimed.

scenes.title: A question with a definite guarantee
scenes.narration: Start with a polynomial whose roots are distinct and real. As its coefficients follow a specified heat equation, those roots move and may collide. We can prove an interval during which no collision is possible. This is a guarantee about a finite mathematical system, with a checker that others can reuse.
screenLines: Input: a finite polynomial with distinct real roots
Output: a guaranteed interval before any collision
Novelty of the bound has not been established
scenes.status: A PRECISE FINITE-POLYNOMIAL RESULT

scenes.narration: The equation is P sub t equals minus P sub z z. We start at time zero and decrease t. For clarity, the animation uses positive elapsed duration u, equal to minus t. The polynomial evolution is a terminating derivative sum, so we can compute its coefficients exactly without Euler steps.

The sum stops at j = floor(n/2)

scenes.title: Three measurements of the starting roots
scenes.narration: Sort the initial roots. Record their number n, the smallest adjacent gap m, and the diameter D zero, from the leftmost root to the rightmost. Our running example has roots minus three, minus one, one, and three. There are four roots, the minimum gap is two, and the diameter is six.

scenes.status: THE INITIAL ROOTS MUST BE DISTINCT AND REAL

scenes.title: An exactly solved moving-root example
scenes.narration: For these four roots, the evolving polynomial is shown here. Substituting w equals z squared reduces its root equation to a quadratic. That calculation proves the first collisions occur at elapsed duration two thirds. At that instant the polynomial becomes z squared minus one, squared: two double roots, at minus one and one.
screenLines: All four roots are real exactly when t ≥ −2/3
First collision: u = 2/3, at z = −1 and z = 1
scenes.status: EXACT ALGEBRA • NOT A COLLISION GUESSED FROM PIXELS

scenes.title: Begin with the two-root baseline
scenes.narration: An isolated pair with gap m has squared gap m squared minus eight u. Its collision duration is exactly m squared over eight. In a larger system, this gives a conservative first guarantee using the smallest starting gap. For the quartic that duration is one half. The other roots let us improve this guarantee.
screenLines: A lower bound on collision time, not the exact time
scenes.status: EXACT FOR TWO ROOTS • A BASELINE FOR MORE ROOTS

scenes.title: Every root contributes to the motion
scenes.narration: Differentiate the equation saying that P is zero at a moving root. Factoring the polynomial then expresses that root's velocity as a sum over all the other roots. This is established heat-flow mathematics. The important change from a local guess is that the interactions outside the nearest pair remain in the calculation.
screenLines: These derivatives are with respect to t, not u
scenes.status: ESTABLISHED ROOT DYNAMICS • VALID BEFORE COLLISION

scenes.title: Track the gap, including exterior roots
scenes.narration: Take adjacent roots a and b, and square their separation to obtain y. Subtracting their velocities gives this exact identity. The quantity S sums the influence of every exterior root. Adjacency makes each denominator positive. In elapsed time u, the minus eight term contracts the gap, while the interaction term offsets part of that contraction.
scenes.status: ADJACENT PAIRS ARE ESSENTIAL TO THE SIGN

scenes.title: Turn the interactions into a usable bound
scenes.narration: As t decreases before a collision, the extreme roots move inward, so their diameter never exceeds its initial value. Each exterior-root denominator is therefore at most D zero squared. There are n minus two such terms. This gives a positive lower bound, kappa, for the interaction sum without solving every root trajectory.
screenLines: D(t) ≤ D₀ for t ≤ 0 before collision
scenes.status: FINITE DIAMETER CONTROLS ALL EXTERIOR INTERACTIONS

scenes.title: A formula for guaranteed collision-free time
scenes.narration: Solve the comparison equation starting from the smallest squared gap. Its value stays below every actual adjacent squared gap. The displayed duration T is where that lower bound reaches zero. Before T, every gap remains positive. For our example, T is about zero point five three zero zero two four, improving the one-half baseline.
scenes.status: THEOREM FOR EVERY ADMISSIBLE FINITE POLYNOMIAL

scenes.title: Why the argument does not assume its conclusion
scenes.narration: The velocity formulas initially apply only while roots are distinct and real. Suppose a first collision occurred before the guaranteed duration. The positive gap bound would forbid it. Roots cannot escape to infinity in finite time because the monic polynomial's coefficients stay bounded. Distinct real roots therefore continue throughout the claimed interval.

An earlier collision would require a zero gap
The bound keeps every gap strictly positive

scenes.title: Use the shrinking diameter for a stronger estimate
scenes.narration: We can retain more information. The extreme-root equations bound the rate at which the squared diameter shrinks in elapsed time. Writing d for its initial square, the diameter squared is at most d minus B u. This smaller denominator strengthens the lower bound on exterior interactions as time advances toward collision.

scenes.status: A TIME-DEPENDENT COMPARISON EQUATION

scenes.title: The stronger duration still has a closed formula
scenes.narration: Integrating the time-dependent comparison gives the stronger duration shown here. Gap packing guarantees that eta lies strictly between zero and one, so the expression is defined. The proof shows this duration exceeds the constant-diameter guarantee. For our quartic it is about zero point five three nine seven one nine. It remains a lower bound on the collision duration.

scenes.title: A guarantee ending is not a collision occurring
scenes.narration: Compare the three guaranteed durations with the exact quartic collision. The strongest certificate ends near zero point five four, but the actual collision is at two thirds. At duration zero point six, all four roots are still real and distinct. Being outside a certificate means that certificate is silent; it does not mean the polynomial has failed.

scenes.title: Use the solved quartic to test local predictors
scenes.narration: The quartic also provides a benchmark with a known answer. A frozen quadratic approximation at the origin predicts a collision there at duration nine twentieths. The exact polynomial at that point is instead two hundred forty-three over one hundred, not zero. This reveals omitted higher-order terms and gives a concrete test for any proposed improved predictor.

scenes.title: Know which changes preserve the guarantee
scenes.narration: Translate every root and the durations stay the same. Scale every root by a nonzero real factor a and the durations multiply by a squared. Repeated roots violate the starting assumptions. Degree two has its own exact pair formula. An arbitrary coefficient motion, or rounded measurements treated as exact roots, is a different problem.
screenLines: Translation: same gaps and same guaranteed duration
Scale roots by a: durations scale by a²
Repeated roots are excluded; degree two is separate
The checker certifies the exact rational inputs supplied
scenes.status: TEST DOMAIN, UNITS, AND THE SPECIFIED HEAT EQUATION

scenes.title: Where the connection to RH actually lies
scenes.narration: The Riemann entire function has a heat deformation called H sub t, with the same heat sign. Its zeros are all real exactly when t is at least a threshold, Lambda. RH is equivalent to Lambda being at most zero. Rodgers and Tao proved Lambda is at least zero. Thus RH is equivalent to Lambda equaling zero. Shared zero dynamics connect the questions.
screenLines: All zeros of H_t are real exactly when t ≥ Λ
Together: RH is equivalent to Λ = 0
scenes.status: AN ESTABLISHED CONNECTION • NOT AN RH ADVANCE BY THIS PROJECT

diagramData.riemannThreshold: All zeros real exactly for t ≥ Λ

scenes.title: The missing step is control of the infinite system
scenes.narration: Our certificate uses finitely many roots and a finite diameter. The Riemann flow has infinitely many zeros, so an extension needs rigorous control of distant zeros and convergence of their interactions. Assuming every zero is real at time zero would assume RH. A uniform real-root interval below zero would contradict the known lower bound on Lambda. The open task is control toward zero from a known-real regime.
screenLines: Finite diameter + finite root list do not cover all zeros
Required: justified infinite interactions and distant-zero bounds
Assuming all H₀ zeros real would already assume RH
Seek control toward t = 0 from a known-real regime
scenes.status: NO RH ADVANCE, PRIME SHORTCUT, OR NOVELTY HAS BEEN ESTABLISHED
